extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, paralegals, and third‑party requesters preparing and filing ex parte reexamination requests at the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing an ex parte reexamination request using USPTO EFS‑Web (procedural requirements, required and recommended supporting documents, EFS‑Web filing steps, fees, timelines, and post‑filing actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must raise a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) based on prior art patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNQ is the threshold for instituting ex parte reexamination; unlike an IPR petition, a reexam request can raise double patenting. After the request is filed, ex parte reexamination typically involves only the patent owner and the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to use EFS-Web (registration/sponsorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use EFS‑Web, you must either be a registered practitioner or be sponsored by a registered practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be sponsored, set up an account with my.uspto.gov and enable two‑factor authentication. For registered practitioners, the sponsorship page is at https://patentcenter-sponsorships.uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet (PTO/SB/57) contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/57 is a checklist for the reexam request that you’re about to file and must include patent and claims to be reexamined, identity of requester (optional), fee information, service address of patent owner, and related litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover sheet to capture basic filing metadata and fee info before submitting the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required components of the Request for Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(1)); (2) an identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(2)); (3) a detailed explanation of how to apply the prior art to each claim; and (4) a certification of no IPR, PGR, or CBM estoppel (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(2), § 1.510(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element is required by regulation—prepare the claim‑by‑claim explanations and the estoppel certification carefully to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended components of the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended items include an exhibit list that assigns a unique number to each supporting document and an explanation of how to construe the claims in light of any patent owner statements filed in other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cite patent owner statements (e.g., litigation claim construction briefs, PTAB briefs, office action responses), those statements must be filed with the request (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(2)). An exhibit list improves organization and tribunal navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit list numbering convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an IPR‑style exhibit list: the copy of the patent to be reexamined is Ex. 1001, its file history is Ex. 1002, etc.; for a second request start the exhibit list with Ex. 1101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a unique exhibit number to each supporting document and place a slipsheet on each exhibit with its exhibit number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required supporting documents: prior art and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide copies of the prior art patents and printed publications used in the reexamination request, including translations of the 'necessary and pertinent' portions of foreign‑language references (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include translations for any foreign references where pertinent and ensure copies are legible and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) listing relied materials
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement (IDS) listing all prior art patents, printed publications, and all other materials relied upon in the request is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include expert declarations, librarian declarations, translations, patent owner statements, and other supporting materials in or referenced by the IDS as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the entire patent to be reexamined
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the 'entire patent' to be reexamined, including all certificates and disclaimers, must be filed (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the full printed patent document and any associated certificates/disclaimers to ensure the examiner has the correct patent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For third‑party requests, a certificate of service on the patent owner is required (37 C.F.R. § 1.510(b)(5)). The certificate must list all documents filed with the USPTO (including the Certificate of Service itself), the method of service, and the name and address of all parties served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve the patent owner at the patent’s correspondence address in Public PAIR. Serving the patent owner’s litigation counsel is optional but a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended supporting documents (additional evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended items include a copy of the patent’s file history, expert declarations, 'librarian' declarations to establish NPL status, claim charts summarizing each proposed rejection, and any litigation claim construction orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are not strictly required but materially strengthen the request and make the examiner’s work easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and page thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees: $12,600 for > 40 pages; $6,300 for ≤ 40 pages (if properly typeset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm correct fee based on properly counted pages and typesetting; incorrect fees can affect filing acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: File organization and formatting (slipsheets, file sizes, PDF/A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Put all documents you plan to file in a single folder, place a slipsheet on each exhibit with its exhibit number, and if any exhibit exceeds 25 MB, split it into multiple parts and give each part its own slipsheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save every document as either a PDF/A (preferred) or an 'image' PDF made by printing the PDF as images within Adobe Acrobat. Split large exhibits (give each part a slipsheet, e.g., Ex. 1001 part 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attaching documents in EFS-Web (upload steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: To attach documents: Step 1 choose a file; Step 2 select category and document description; Step 3 click 'Add File' to add another file; Step 4 repeat until all files attached; Step 5 click 'Upload and Validate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to select the correct document category and description for each file to ensure proper handling and review by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload and validate / review documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After attaching files, use the 'Upload and Validate' and reviewing screens to confirm documents uploaded correctly before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify each uploaded exhibit, category, and pagination in the review step to avoid filing defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting embedded fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embedded font causes upload/validation problems: remove the offending file, then try—(1) resave the PDF as a PDF/A; (2) print the PDF as an image PDF, then reattach; (3) print as an image PDF then save that as a PDF/A and reattach; (4) if all else fails, print a hard copy, scan it, and save the scan as a PDF/A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the steps in order; converting to image PDFs or scanning will avoid embedded font issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting paper size and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure every page in the PDF is in portrait orientation instead of landscape and print to PDF using the 'Shrink oversized pages' setting if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct page orientation and sizing before uploading to avoid validation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedure after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: After clicking 'submit' you will be taken to the payment page. If you have a USPTO Financial Manager Account, log in and select a payment method; if not, you can continue as a guest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete payment to finalize the filing—ensure payment method is ready at submission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control number and confirmation number use
rubrics_metrics.description: You will get a filing receipt that provides the Reexamination Control Number (90/XXX,XXX) and a four‑digit Confirmation Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Reexamination Control Number to access the reexamination proceeding in PAIR or Patent Center and use both numbers for all subsequent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving the patent owner (physical delivery and optional email)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must physically send the request and supporting documents to the patent owner (e.g., via USPS, FedEx, or UPS); you can save the request and supporting documents to a flash drive, CD, or DVD instead of sending everything in paper. Serving a courtesy copy via email is optional but a best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the method and address in the Certificate of Service match actual service; consider emailing a courtesy copy to litigation counsel where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO SNQ decision timing and filing moratorium
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO must decide whether the request presents an SNQ within three months of the request’s filing date. With a few limited exceptions, the requester cannot file anything else during the course of the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the initial SNQ determination within three months and plan client communications and litigation strategy accordingly given the moratorium on requester filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Rehearing of Denial timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO determines the request does not present an SNQ, it will deny reexamination. The requester can file a petition for rehearing within one month of the decision denying reexamination (37 C.F.R. § 1.515(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and file rehearing petitions promptly if institution is denied and you wish to pursue reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement on Decision ordering reexamination (patent owner deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO finds that the request does present an SNQ, the patent owner has two months from the decision ordering reexamination to file an optional statement. The statement can include claim amendments (37 C.F.R. § 1.530).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should consider whether to submit an optional statement and any claim amendments within the two‑month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to Statement on Decision ordering reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner files an optional statement on the SNQ decision, the requester can file a reply within two months of the statement (37 C.F.R. § 1.535).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare reply arguments and updated exhibits within the two‑month reply period to address any patent owner amendments or arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Terminate or Vacate: grounds and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner can petition to terminate a reexamination or vacate an order granting reexamination on grounds such as IPR, CBM, or PGR estoppel and harassment by requester. A petition to terminate or vacate based on IPR, CBM, or PGR estoppel must be filed within two months of the decision ordering reexamination (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.181‑1.183, 1.540; MPEP 2246).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on estoppel grounds, file termination/vacatur petitions promptly within the two‑month window; include supporting evidence of estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Petition to Terminate/Vacate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to terminate or vacate is filed, call the Examiner and the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff ASAP to explain opposition; a response is due within two weeks of the petition (MPEP 2246).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act immediately on petitions to terminate/vacate—coordinate with examiner and CRU and file substantive responses within the short two‑week deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action response periods and concurrent litigation shortening
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, the Patent Owner has two months to respond to a non‑final office action and two months to respond to a final office action. However, those response periods can be shortened to one month if there is concurrent litigation (37 C.F.R. § 1.550(b); MPEP 2263, 2272).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor concurrent litigation status; if concurrent litigation is ongoing, prepare to meet shortened response deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for extension of time
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for extension of time must be filed before the due date for the office action response and must show good cause for the extension (37 C.F.R. § 1.550(c); MPEP 2265). In third‑party reexams, one month is typical; two months are rarely granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File extension requests early and include persuasive good cause facts—do not expect long extensions in third‑party reexams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure during reexamination and IDS filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Owner remains under a duty of disclosure during the reexamination and should file Information Disclosure Statements accordingly. Copies of foreign references and non‑patent literature must be filed with the IDS (37 C.F.R. § 1.555).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners must continually update IDSs with relevant references discovered during reexamination to satisfy the duty of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of concurrent proceedings obligation and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester has the opportunity, and the Patent Owner has the obligation, to keep the USPTO apprised of relevant related proceedings. A notice of concurrent proceedings can be filed at any time (37 C.F.R. § 1.565(a); MPEP 2280, 2282).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File notices of concurrent proceedings to inform the USPTO of related litigation or proceedings that may affect claim construction or estoppel issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner appellate filing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent owner appellate filings consult MPEP 1204, 2273, and 2274 for applicable procedures and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP references for appellate timing, content, and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every filing requires a certificate of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that every filing in the reexamination proceeding needs a certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the Certificate of Service for every submission and ensure accuracy of listed documents, methods, and recipient addresses.
